title: Apertus 1.5: From Open Text Models to Open Multimodal Reasoners
data_curation: Only openly available, license-reviewed data; robots.txt opt-outs applied retroactively; PII removed. Text SFT mix has 3,707,851 samples (math & reasoning 25.6%, multilingual 25.8%, code & functions 19.8%, regional 15.4%), decontaminated against 595 benchmarks by n-gram matching with manual review (and perceptual hashing against ~950K benchmark images). Capability filtering: an auxiliary non-thinking 8B SFT checkpoint samples 8 answers per verifiable prompt. Prompts it solves at least once stay trace-free; the rest get verified reasoning traces from Kimi-K2.6, Qwen3.6-27B, Gemma-4-31B and MiniMax-M2.7. Tool data is execution-verified only (Toucan, EnvScaler, OpenSeeker, Jupyter Agent); tool declarations are injected into 131,557 non-tool chats. The production image SFT pool has 43.9M sequences / 143.4B tokens. RL uses 349,300 prompts (math, IF, code, translated Reasoning Gym, vision, tabular, LEXam). DPO uses 245,898 Dolci-Instruct-DPO prompts, scored by a Qwen3-235B rubric judge with MaxMin pairing.
curriculum: Starts from Apertus 1.0 checkpoints. Continued pretraining (4T tokens for 8B, 2T for 70B) has four stages: (1) unpaired image/audio/text with all-modality targets; (2) paired image-text and audio-transcript data with text-only targets; (3) a cooldown on higher-quality math/code/translation data plus ~3B instruction tokens; (4) long-context extension 8K→32K→65K→131K→262K (50-63B tokens per step, with synthetic CWE/DocOrder/needle tasks). Post-training then runs SFT (16K context) → long-context SFT at 262K (needed because RULER@262K fell from 54.8 to 8.3 after SFT) → RLVR → DPO (online DPO only for the 8B; offline then online for the 70B) → SDPO charter alignment (8B only). Thinking is a chat-template flag, not a separate model.
method: Discrete-token early fusion: images (512x512 → 1,024 tokens) and audio (2,400 tokens/min) enter through the tokenizer, the LM head stays text-only, and the architecture is unchanged (AdEMAMix optimizer, Goldfish loss). SFT runs at a constant LR (8B: 6e-5, batch 256, ~159B tokens; 70B: 1e-5, batch 1,024). RL uses a fully asynchronous verl fork with 8 rollouts/prompt, leave-one-out advantages, zero-variance group filtering, asymmetric clipping (0.2, 0.28), geometric-mean loss aggregation, no KL, LR 1e-6 and no length penalty. Rewards come from Math-Verify, IF constraint checkers, sandboxed tests and exact match, with answers emitted via an answer tool. Training is 480 steps (~1M trajectories) for 8B and 180 for 70B, on mixed thinking-on/off prompts. Tool-use prompts were dropped from RL because of server bottlenecks. Offline DPO is length-normalized (β=25, LR 1e-6). Online DPO uses β=0.1, a Qwen3.6-27B helpfulness judge and 12/8 rollouts. SDPO distills a judge-feedback-conditioned teacher (top-64 reverse KL, LR 1e-7, 117 steps).
eval_metrics: Roughly 50-task text suite (knowledge, IF, math, code, multilingual/cultural, safety, function calling, charter alignment), plus held-out benchmarks used to detect overfitting, image/audio suites (LMMs-Eval, VLMEvalKit), RULER/HELMET long context, and AIME mean@8 with a 32,768-token thinking budget. Apertus 1.5 8B (thinking off) scores MMLU 70.5, MMLU-Pro 48.8, IFEval 87.1, Multi-IF 83.7, IFBench 35.3, AlpacaEval LC 47.2, MATH-500 51.2. With thinking on: MATH-500 71.4, IFBench 44.3, AIME24 22.9, AIME25 23.8, and MMMU roughly +10. The preference stage raises the dev-suite average from 49.3 to 54.8 (8B) and from 55.3 to 61.2 (70B).
key_results: Apertus 1.5 8B is the strongest of all compared 8B-class models (open-weight included) on instruction following (IFEval 87.1, Multi-IF 83.7). Thinking lifts its MATH-500 from 51.2 to 71.4 and AIME24 from 7.5 to 22.9. The 70B improves over Apertus 1.0 on every benchmark but trails open-weight peers such as Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4.
evolution_note: Builds on Apertus 1.0 (2025, 15T tokens, 1000+ languages) as a fully open model upgraded in place to image and audio input via discrete-token early fusion. Its post-training borrows from the open-recipe lineage: OLMo 3's Dolci prompts and IFTrain constraints, DAPO-style asymmetric clipping, and online DPO with MaxMin pairing (Delta Learning). It also introduces SDPO self-distillation for charter alignment. Its lessons include filtering reasoning traces by what the model already solves, adding long-context SFT to recover retrieval lost in SFT, and running offline DPO before online DPO at 70B. All are released with open data, code and checkpoints.
